note: The record of what Linear held for each project at cutover. projects.name: 1991chat — Chat front-end
projects.summary: Hand-built React chat UI on top of the existing skeleton + @services layer. Ordered via RADIO.
projects.description:
Implement the chat UI by hand, on top of the existing `front/` skeleton.

**Already done (do NOT rebuild):** the whole `@services` layer — `chat.service.ts` streams via `fetch` + `getReader` with `AbortSignal`; `conversation.service.ts` CRUD; `ApiError` + CSRF/401/403 handling; SSE parser; all wire DTOs in `*.types.ts`. The app shell/sidebar chrome is also done.

**To build:** the presentational components (`Message`, `MessageList`, `ChatDisplay`, `Prompt`, `Sidebar`), the client-side state owner (`useChat`), conversation routing, and UX polish — plus one small backend+front contract change (<issue id="a4fe279c-7c4d-4d0f-b1cd-9d2417dc96ed" href="https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-18/sse-contract-carry-message-ids-in-the-open-frame-backend-front-service">COS-18</issue>).

Tickets are ordered (`01 · …` → `13 · …`) and linked with blocked-by relations; each carries a `RADIO:` tag. <issue id="a4fe279c-7c4d-4d0f-b1cd-9d2417dc96ed" href="https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-18/sse-contract-carry-message-ids-in-the-open-frame-backend-front-service">COS-18</issue> is the only backend ticket and slots in before the `useChat` hook (ticket 06).

**How ids stay in sync (Option C):** both message ids are generated server-side before the first token. <issue id="a4fe279c-7c4d-4d0f-b1cd-9d2417dc96ed" href="https://linear.app/cosmokaat/issue/COS-18/sse-contract-carry-message-ids-in-the-open-frame-backend-front-service">COS-18</issue> sends them down in the `open` SSE frame, so the front stamps the real database ids the moment streaming starts — an optimistic bubble shows instantly with a temporary id and is swapped for the real one on `open`. On `done` the front just marks the message complete. No refetch, no temp-id reconciliation; the front is in sync by construction.

projects.name: Exalus
projects.summary: Extract PFA's generic UI building blocks (dataviz, month-picker…) into app-agnostic modules, reusable in other projects through a shadcn-style registry (copy-and-own).
projects.description:
**Goal**

Pull out of PFA the UI building blocks that have nothing PFA-specific about them — the hand-rolled dataviz lib, the month-picker, and whatever follows — and make them installable in any other project.

**Principle: copy-and-own, not a package**

The chosen mechanism is a **shadcn-style registry**: the consuming project runs `pnpm dlx shadcn add <url>`, the code is copied into its tree and owned locally. It re-themes and edits freely.

What this avoids: npm publishing, git packages, monorepo / pnpm workspace, tsup or rollup builds, and the whole versioning ceremony that comes with them. For a solo dev that is cost without benefit. A real package is reserved for the many-projects or open-source case, not this one.

Two things make the registry the natural fit here: shadcn is already wired up on the PFA side (`front/components.json`), and since Tailwind v4 is CSS-first, the tokens have to travel as files regardless — which a registry handles natively via `cssVars` / `css`.

**Scope**

One registry item per shippable unit, each carrying its own files, registry dependencies, and slice of tokens/keyframes. First candidates: the dataviz primitives (donut, bar chart, line chart, stacked bar, progress track) and the month-picker.

Out of scope: application glue (adapters, URL state, copy) — it gets rewritten per host project and stays in PFA.

**Timing rule**

Nothing gets built while reuse is speculative. The registry goes up the day a real second project needs it (≈ one afternoon). In the meantime, only "registry-ready" hygiene happens, and only opportunistically when passing through the files concerned — never as a dedicated refactor.

**Not to be confused with**

`design-sync` / `.design-sync` publishes the design system to Claude Design: that is a design-time tool, not an installable module. The two efforts stay separate.

projects.name: Iknos
projects.summary: Self-hosted monitoring for the apps on ks-b: ECS logs, Prometheus metrics, grouped errors and alerts, with no lock-in.
projects.description:
**Iknos** is a small self-hosted monitoring tool for the apps running on ks-b, starting with PFA. No Docker, no SaaS, no agent to install inside the apps.

## Principle

The tool is disposable, the interfaces are not. A monitored app only ever does two standard things:

* write **ECS-structured NDJSON logs to stdout** (pino + `@elastic/ecs-pino-format`), which PM2 already persists to files;
* expose `GET /metrics` **in Prometheus text format**, next to a `/health` endpoint that actually checks its dependencies.

An app never talks to Iknos. Replacing Iknos with Grafana Loki, Prometheus, Elastic or an OTLP pipeline later means swapping the collector — Alloy/Promtail reads the very same files, Prometheus scrapes the very same endpoint — with **zero change in the monitored apps**. No SDK, no adapter, no lock-in.

## Architecture

Two PM2 processes on ks-b, one MySQL database, one Redis prefix. No new infrastructure.

* `iknos-collector` — Node daemon. Tails the PM2 log files (offset + inode persisted, rotation-safe), scrapes `/metrics` every 15s, probes `/health` every 30s, samples host CPU/RAM/disk and `pm2 jlist`, fingerprints errors into issues, evaluates alert rules, runs nightly retention and hourly rollups.
* `iknos-ui` — Next app on its own subdomain. Server components read MySQL through Prisma; only mutations and live tail go through route handlers. Session auth copied from PFA (httpOnly cookie, Redis-backed rolling session, CSRF token on unsafe verbs, bcrypt hashes). Design system copied from PFA (copy-and-own, no shared package).

Any PM2 app on the host is collected without instrumentation — non-JSON lines degrade to a plain message. Apps that emit ECS get the full feature set.

## Scope, v1

* **Logs** — full-text search plus filters (service, level, route, status, time range), live tail, and request correlation through `trace.id`.
* **Metrics** — request rate, error rate, p95 latency per route, Node runtime internals, host CPU/RAM/disk, PM2 restart counts.
* **Issues** — errors deduplicated by fingerprint, stable across deploys, with occurrence counts, stack traces and links back to their logs.
* **Alerts** — rules evaluated by the collector, persisted with a severity and a state, consulted in the UI. Nothing is pushed anywhere in v1; you come and look.

## Out of scope for now

Notification channels (email, Telegram), distributed traces, HTTP ingestion from other hosts, per-user roles. The log schema and the database schema are chosen so that each of these is additive rather than a rewrite.

## Stack

Node 22, TypeScript, pnpm workspace, Prisma 7 with the `@prisma/adapter-mariadb` driver against **MySQL** (the same pairing PFA already uses), Next (App Router), Tailwind v4 with the PFA design tokens, Biome, Vitest, nginx + PM2. MySQL and Redis are already running on ks-b.

projects.name: Spira
projects.summary: Self-hosted single-user ticketing app replacing Linear: per-project ticket prefixes, legacy COS-xxx references preserved.
projects.description:
## Goal

Replace Linear with a self-hosted, single-user ticketing app. The paid plan carries a lot that goes unused, and the workspace-level prefix means all six projects share one `COS-` counter — `COS-177` is a PFA ticket and `COS-201` is a 3D engine ticket, with nothing in the identifier saying so.

The UI copies Linear's deliberately. This is a personal tool, never a product.

## Two hard requirements

**Per-project prefixes.** New issues get `PFA-1`, `3DE-1`, `SPI-1` — first three letters of the project, editable and unique.

**Legacy references keep resolving.** Hundreds of `COS-xxx` identifiers live in commit messages, code comments and PR descriptions. On import every issue is renumbered under its project key, and its original identifier is kept in a `legacyIdentifier` column: both are indexed, both are searchable, the row renders **PFA-12** with a subdued `COS-177` beside it, and `/issue/COS-177` redirects to the new URL.

## Architecture

One Next.js 16 app on ks-b behind nginx — no separate API service. Reads go straight through Prisma from Server Components; every write goes through a REST route handler under `/api`, because the MCP connector needs a callable HTTP surface and one write path beats two implementations of the same rules.

Auth is PFA's model transposed off Express: httpOnly `spira.sid` cookie, session in Redis, CSRF token minted into the session and checked against `X-CSRF-Token` on unsafe verbs, bcryptjs, single seeded account with no signup. Middleware only does a cookie-presence redirect — authorisation is enforced by `requireSession()` on the Node runtime, since Redis cannot run on Edge.

Stack: Prisma 7 + MySQL, Redis, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, lucide-react, nuqs, zod v4, react-hook-form, TanStack Query, Biome, vitest + Playwright. No lodash, no zustand, no axios.

## Model

Epics are ordinary issues flagged `isEpic`, so they get their own identifier, description and status. Other issues point at one via `epicId`. An epic cannot sit inside an epic — the hierarchy is exactly one level, with no recursion anywhere. Blocking is stored once as `A blocks B`; "blocked by" is the same row read backwards, so the two views cannot disagree.

## In v1

Projects, issues, statuses (Backlog / Todo / In Progress / In Review / Done / Canceled), multiple labels per issue, epics, blocking relations, filters, saved views, list layout, project description page, markdown descriptions with cross-reference chips, search, CSV migration from Linear, MCP connector, ks-b deployment.

## Not in v1

Board layout, drag & drop, comments, activity history, command palette, keyboard shortcuts, milestones, cycles, initiatives, attachments, assignees, estimates, multi-user.

## The one irreversible step

Linear's CSV export contains descriptions but **not comment threads and not issue relations**. Both vanish with the workspace. Taking a complete raw GraphQL export is therefore the first migration ticket, ahead of the importer, and happens regardless of v1 not rendering comments.

Full spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-29-spira-design.md`

projects.name: Worldweathr
projects.summary: Daily sky log — declare the weather over your city, compare it to the forecast, and see everyone ranked by participation.
projects.description:
WorldWeathr is a daily *sky log*. Once a day, in your city, you declare what the sky is actually doing — from six conditions, plus whether it's windy — say how it feels, optionally give the exact temperature, and log it. The app then shows what the official forecast said and keeps score of how often you and the forecast agree.

The social layer is not a feed and has no follows. Every connected user appears on a single Community board ranked by how much they log, each attaching one preset mood — no free text, so there is nothing to moderate.

## Three levels of commitment

* **Guest** — no account. Pick a city, log the sky, see the forecast comparison, browse the Community board. Their logs count, at 0.25 weight.
* **Member** — account with a chosen @handle. Full History and Stats, full weight.
* Everything a guest logged carries over the moment they sign up.

## Stack

* **front/** — Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/Radix, TanStack Query 5, Zod 4, react-hook-form, biome, vitest + Playwright
* **api/** — NestJS 11, Prisma 7 + MySQL 8, express-session + Redis, bcryptjs, class-validator, biome, jest + supertest
* **prod** — [https://worldweathr.com](<https://worldweathr.com>), nginx same-origin, atomic releases (same deploy scripts as pfa)

## Design

Claude Design project `fa45f334-3653-4458-a502-1c9f1dab2f8f`, file `Skyshare.dc.html`. **Turn 6 is authoritative.** Turn 1B/1C are rejected visual directions; Turn 5 (Friends feed) is superseded by Turn 6 (Community) and is not built.

⚠️ The design was drawn under the old product name **Skyshare**. That name survives only as the design artefact's filename — the wordmark and all shipped copy say **WorldWeathr**.

## Spec

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-worldweathr-design.md` in the repo. Read it before starting any ticket — it carries the schema, the security model, the WMO mapping and the guest-mode rules.

projects.name: Zeus
projects.summary: Fleet control plane for the apps on ks-b (1991computer): port registry, status, start/stop, port reassignment.
projects.description:
**Zeus** is the control plane / mission-control for every app running on the `ks-b` VPS (`1991computer`). Today, managing them means manual SSH + `pm2` + hand-edited nginx configs, and the port map lives in people's heads — which is how `6400` nearly got double-booked. Zeus makes the fleet observable and controllable from one place.

## Problem

* ~6+ apps on ks-b (pfa, bkmk, conway, 1991chat, hiwaysim, worldweathr, …), each a front and/or API running under pm2 behind nginx.
* **No single source of truth for ports** → collisions and guesswork.
* Start / stop / restart = manual SSH + `pm2`.
* Changing a port = edit the ecosystem config + nginx + reload, by hand, error-prone.

## What Zeus does (phased)

1. **Port registry** — the authoritative list of every app's front port + reserved API block (`6N00–6N99` per API, front on `30xx`). Enforces the convention and blocks collisions. Replaces the manual ports doc.
2. **Status dashboard** — live per-app health from `pm2 jlist` (online/stopped, port, uptime, restarts, cpu/mem) + optional HTTP health ping.
3. **Process control** — start / stop / restart / reload each app via pm2, from the UI, with confirmation + audit log.
4. **Port (re)assignment** — change an app's port safely: rewrite its `ecosystem.config.cjs` + nginx `proxy_pass` + reload both, atomically, with rollback.
5. **Later** — tail pm2 logs; maybe trigger the existing deploy scripts.

## Architecture (draft — finalised in the design ticket)

* Runs **on ks-b** — it needs local access to pm2, nginx and the filesystem. Same stack family as the other apps: NestJS API + Next dashboard.
* API shells out to `pm2` (jlist/start/stop/restart), reads/writes ecosystem + nginx configs, and runs `nginx -t && nginx -s reload` behind a **least-privilege** sudo rule.
* Own ports per the fleet convention: **API block** `6600–6699` **(api** `6600`**), front** `3003` — to confirm & verify-free when we start.

## Security (non-negotiable)

Zeus can start/stop processes and rewrite nginx — a high-value target. It must be:

* **Admin-only**, strong auth (mirror pfa/worldweathr: httpOnly session + CSRF token).
* **Not casually public** — bound internally behind an SSH tunnel, or an IP allowlist + basic auth in front.
* **Fully audited** — every control action logged (who/what/when).
* **Least-privilege** — only the exact sudo commands it needs (nginx reload), nothing broader.

## Status

Backlog. We build this **after** WorldWeathr's early milestones. The manual `ks-b` ports doc we write now becomes Zeus's seed data.
